claims.text: What the strip looks like In V1–V3: horizontal ST depression, tall broad R waves, upright T waves, and a dominant R wave in V2.

claims.text: With ischemic symptoms, horizontal ST depression in V1–V3 should raise suspicion of posterior MI

claims.text: Why: the anterior leads record posterior activity from the front, so the injury pattern inverts — ST elevation becomes ST depression, Q waves become R waves, terminal T inversion becomes an upright T

claims.text: Posterior extension means a much larger infarct, with more risk of LV dysfunction and death
